subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should isolated cron jobs get their own `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or use a delivery-mode-specific default such as denying `message` during announce delivery?
rationale: This decides a public config surface and unattended-execution security boundary, including how existing per-job `toolsAllow` and delivery behavior interact with global tool policy.

options.title: Add explicit cron policy
options.body: Add `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with documented precedence over or under per-job `toolsAllow`, plus schema/types/docs and regression tests.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Treat cron isolated sessions as subagent-like for tool policy while documenting why cron and delegated sessions share the same boundary.

options.title: Use delivery-aware defaults only
options.body: Avoid a new broad config key and instead deny or suppress direct `message` sends for announce delivery unless explicitly allowed.

recommendation.title: Add explicit cron policy
recommendation.body: Add `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with documented precedence over or under per-job `toolsAllow`, plus schema/types/docs and regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across cron delivery/session runtime and shared tool-policy diagnostics, which frame this security boundary.
